article.title: Red Sea rerouting strands wiring-harness containers; Maruti halts two Manesar lines
article.text: Maruti Suzuki India suspended production on two of its Manesar assembly lines after wiring-harness containers routed around the Cape of Good Hope arrived eighteen days late, exhausting the buffer stock the company had built through December. The plant runs on a two-day inventory model for harnesses, which are model-specific and cannot be substituted between platforms. The company said it expects to recover the lost volume within the quarter through additional Saturday shifts. Component suppliers on the affected programmes will see the same volume gap in their own dispatch schedules before the recovery shifts begin.
article.note: The only fixture where a distance-2 company earns a primary slot -- and it earns it on an independently sourced relationship artifact, not on the model's say-so about who supplies whom.

shocks.label: Shipping route disruption
shocks.mechanism: Rerouting around the Cape adds roughly a fortnight of transit, which breaks just-in-time inventory models that hold days rather than weeks of cover

shocks.label: Component supply gap
shocks.mechanism: A stopped assembly programme removes the offtake its component suppliers were scheduled to dispatch against, propagating the volume gap one link down the chain

companies.name: Maruti Suzuki India
companies.mechanism: Two assembly lines are stopped for want of a model-specific harness with only two days of cover, so the volume gap is booked before the recovery shifts can begin
companies.rationale: Company-confirmed line stoppage caused directly by the rerouting delay
